history.period: 16th-17th century (chapel 1566; church elevated later; destroyed by fire 1834)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - this is a 17th-century Roman Catholic church ruin; keep-or-drop decision needed. Jesuit missionaries settled at Sancoale in 1560 and completed the chapel of Nossa Senhora de Saude in 1566, later elevated to a church (one account dates the church building to 1606). The building caught fire in 1834 (some sources say the 18th century - conflict) and today only the baroque frontispiece with composite Corinthian pilasters and bas-reliefs survives, on the banks of the Zuari River, visible from the Agassaim-Cortalim bridge. St. Joseph Vaz (1651-1711), patron saint of Sri Lanka, wrote his famed 'Letter of Bondage' (Escravo de Maria) at this church in August 1677. Declared a national monument by the Portuguese government on 19 March 1937; maintained by the Directorate of Archives and Archaeology. A newer chapel of Our Lady of Health was built behind the facade in 1783. CSV town correction: the ruins are at Sancoale, Mormugao taluka (South Goa), near but not in Vasco da Gama as the CSV claims. Coordinates are approximate (town-level geocode; no POI match).

name: Sancoale Church Ruins
town_description: Sancoale is a coastal town in Mormugao taluka, South Goa, on the banks of the Zuari River a few kilometres from Vasco da Gama. It is the hometown of St. Joseph Vaz (1651-1711), the Goan missionary who is the patron saint of Sri Lanka.
